_comment: Without colour (notes/strange-words-plan.md 4). On the air it is the drain -- the whole Age seen in grey,
every frame, the monochrome step written on purpose. Aimed at anything else that holds a colour it bleaches
that thing white: a white sun, pale grass, clear water. Aimed at the land or the surface it builds or dresses
them from black to white -- concrete, wool, terracotta, the greyer stones -- as `grey` does with grey alone,
and aimed at what grows it takes the flowers out.
A colourless Age does all of it, the land and the surface one Age in ten as `grey`'s are. It never brings a
rainbow or an aurora about (`unaimed_chance_to_apply` 0): naming either's colour would say the Age has one, and one it has
already is seen in grey through the drain. `colourless rainbow`, written on purpose, bleaches a bow.
